import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# The Zeeman conjecture

The Zeeman conjecture asks whether the product of every finite contractible two-dimensional
complex with the closed interval is PL homeomorphic to a collapsible complex. Equivalently, some
iterated derived (barycentric) subdivision of the product must be collapsible.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Zeeman conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeeman_conjecture)
- [Adiprasito and Benedetti, *Subdivisions, shellability, and collapsibility of products*]
  (https://arxiv.org/abs/1202.6606)
-/

namespace ZeemanConjecture

/-- A finite abstract simplicial complex, before imposing the face axioms. An ordering of the
vertices is included in order to choose the standard staircase triangulation of a product with an
interval. -/
structure FiniteSimplicialComplex where
  Vertex : Type
  vertexFintype : Fintype Vertex
  vertexOrder : LinearOrder Vertex
  faces : Finset (Finset Vertex)

attribute [instance] FiniteSimplicialComplex.vertexFintype
  FiniteSimplicialComplex.vertexOrder

namespace FiniteSimplicialComplex

/-- The axioms for a finite abstract simplicial complex whose declared vertex type is exactly its
set of vertices. -/
def IsComplex (K : FiniteSimplicialComplex) : Prop :=
  ∅ ∈ K.faces ∧
    (∀ σ ∈ K.faces, ∀ τ ⊆ σ, τ ∈ K.faces) ∧
    ∀ v : K.Vertex, {v} ∈ K.faces

/-- A simplicial complex is two-dimensional when all its faces have at most three vertices and it
has a face with exactly three vertices. -/
def IsTwoDimensional (K : FiniteSimplicialComplex) : Prop :=
  (∀ σ ∈ K.faces, σ.card ≤ 3) ∧ ∃ σ ∈ K.faces, σ.card = 3

/-- The standard geometric realization of a finite abstract simplicial complex, in barycentric
coordinates indexed by its vertices. -/
def realization (K : FiniteSimplicialComplex) : Set (K.Vertex → ℝ) :=
  {x | (∀ v, 0 ≤ x v) ∧
    (∑ v, x v) = 1 ∧
    Finset.univ.filter (fun v ↦ x v ≠ 0) ∈ K.faces}

/-- A face in the standard staircase triangulation of `K × [0,1]`. -/
def IsIntervalProductFace (K : FiniteSimplicialComplex)
    (σ : Finset (K.Vertex × Fin 2)) : Prop :=
  σ.image Prod.fst ∈ K.faces ∧
    (σ : Set (K.Vertex × Fin 2)).Pairwise
      (fun x y ↦ (x.1 ≤ y.1 ∧ x.2 ≤ y.2) ∨ (y.1 ≤ x.1 ∧ y.2 ≤ x.2))

/-- The standard staircase triangulation of the product of `K` with the closed interval. -/
noncomputable def intervalProduct (K : FiniteSimplicialComplex) : FiniteSimplicialComplex := by
  classical
  exact {
    Vertex := K.Vertex ×ₗ Fin 2
    vertexFintype := inferInstance
    vertexOrder := inferInstance
    faces := Finset.univ.filter K.IsIntervalProductFace }

/-- One elementary simplicial collapse of a face family removes a free codimension-one face and
its unique coface. -/
def ElementaryCollapse {V : Type} [DecidableEq V]
    (A B : Finset (Finset V)) : Prop :=
  ∃ σ ∈ A, ∃ τ ∈ A,
    σ ⊂ τ ∧ τ.card = σ.card + 1 ∧
    (∀ υ ∈ A, σ ⊆ υ → υ = σ ∨ υ = τ) ∧
    B = (A.erase σ).erase τ

/-- A finite simplicial complex is collapsible if elementary collapses reduce its face family to
that of a single vertex. -/
def Collapsible (K : FiniteSimplicialComplex) : Prop :=
  ∃ v : K.Vertex,
    Relation.ReflTransGen ElementaryCollapse K.faces {∅, {v}}

/-- `L` is the derived (barycentric) subdivision of `K`: vertices of `L` correspond to nonempty
faces of `K`, and faces of `L` correspond to chains of such faces. -/
def IsDerivedSubdivision (K L : FiniteSimplicialComplex) : Prop :=
  ∃ e : L.Vertex ≃ {σ : Finset K.Vertex // σ ∈ K.faces ∧ σ.Nonempty},
    ∀ τ : Finset L.Vertex,
      τ ∈ L.faces ↔
        (τ : Set L.Vertex).Pairwise
          (fun x y ↦ (e x).1 ⊆ (e y).1 ∨ (e y).1 ⊆ (e x).1)

/-- `L` is obtained from `K` by applying the derived-subdivision operation finitely many times. -/
inductive IsIteratedDerivedSubdivision :
    FiniteSimplicialComplex → FiniteSimplicialComplex → Prop
  | refl (K) : IsIteratedDerivedSubdivision K K
  | step {K L M} : IsIteratedDerivedSubdivision K L → IsDerivedSubdivision L M →
      IsIteratedDerivedSubdivision K M

/-- PL collapsibility, expressed by the equivalent condition that some iterated derived
subdivision is a collapsible simplicial complex. -/
def PLCollapsible (K : FiniteSimplicialComplex) : Prop :=
  ∃ L, IsIteratedDerivedSubdivision K L ∧ L.Collapsible

end FiniteSimplicialComplex

/--
**Zeeman conjecture.** Given a finite contractible two-dimensional CW (equivalently, finite
polyhedral) complex $K$, is $K \times [0,1]$ PL homeomorphic to a collapsible complex? Here the
conclusion is stated in the equivalent subdivision form: some finite iterated derived subdivision
of a staircase triangulation of $K \times [0,1]$ is collapsible.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 57]
theorem zeeman_conjecture :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ K : FiniteSimplicialComplex,
      K.IsComplex → K.IsTwoDimensional → ContractibleSpace K.realization →
        (K.intervalProduct).PLCollapsible := by
  sorry

end ZeemanConjecture
modeling_decisions: Modeled the finite two-dimensional complex by a finite abstract simplicial complex and used its standard barycentric-coordinate geometric realization for the contractibility hypothesis. This follows the background article and Adiprasito–Benedetti's equivalent finite simplicial/polyhedral formulation; Mathlib's classical CW-complex API has no notions of PL homeomorphism, subdivision, or collapse.
Interpreted “two-dimensional” as dimension exactly two: every face has at most three vertices and at least one face has three vertices.
Interpreted the question as a yes/no proposition using `answer(sorry) ↔ ...`, as required by repository conventions.

Interpreted “collapsible” in the PL sense via the cited equivalent condition that some finite iterated derived subdivision is simplicially collapsible, rather than requiring the initially chosen product triangulation to collapse.

Used the standard ordered staircase triangulation of the product with `[0,1]`. The included linear order merely chooses this triangulation; every finite vertex set can be ordered, and the resulting triangulations represent the same PL product.
Defined an elementary collapse as removal of a free codimension-one face together with its unique coface, and collapsibility as a finite sequence ending at the one-vertex complex.

/-!
# Zeeman conjecture

The conjecture asks whether the product of every finite contractible two-dimensional complex with
an interval is PL homeomorphic to a collapsible complex. Here this is expressed by asking for a
finite collapsible simplicial triangulation of the product polyhedron; in particular, no fixed
triangulation of the product is required to collapse.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: Zeeman conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeeman_conjecture)
- [Adiprasito and Benedetti, *Subdivisions, shellability, and collapsibility of products*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1202.6606)
-/

namespace ZeemanConjecture

open Geometry Set

/-- `G` is obtained from `F` by an elementary simplicial collapse: a free face `σ` and its
unique strict coface `τ` are deleted. -/
def ElementaryCollapse {V : Type*} (F G : Set (Finset V)) : Prop :=
  ∃ σ τ, σ ∈ F ∧ τ ∈ F ∧ σ ⊂ τ ∧ (∀ ρ ∈ F, σ ⊂ ρ → ρ = τ) ∧
    G = F \ {σ, τ}

/-- A simplicial complex is collapsible if elementary collapses reduce its face set to one vertex. -/
def IsCollapsible {E : Type*} [AddCommGroup E] [Module ℝ E]
    (K : SimplicialComplex ℝ E) : Prop :=
  ∃ v, Relation.ReflTransGen ElementaryCollapse K.faces {{v}}

/-- A subset of a real vector space is PL-collapsible if it has a finite collapsible simplicial
triangulation. -/
def IsPLCollapsible {E : Type*} [AddCommGroup E] [Module ℝ E] (s : Set E) : Prop :=
  ∃ K : SimplicialComplex ℝ E, K.faces.Finite ∧ K.space = s ∧ IsCollapsible K

/--
**Zeeman conjecture.** Given any finite contractible two-dimensional polyhedral complex $K$, is
$K \times [0,1]$ PL homeomorphic to a collapsible complex? Equivalently, does its product
polyhedron admit some finite collapsible simplicial triangulation? The conclusion does not assert
that any prescribed product triangulation is itself collapsible.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 57]
theorem zeeman_conjecture :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
        (K : SimplicialComplex ℝ E),
        K.faces.Finite →
        (∀ σ ∈ K.faces, σ.card ≤ 3) →
        (∃ σ ∈ K.faces, σ.card = 3) →
        ContractibleSpace K.space →
        IsPLCollapsible (K.space ×ˢ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) := by
  sorry

end ZeemanConjecture

Used Mathlib's `ContractibleSpace` on the underlying polyhedron `K.space` for contractibility.

Modeled the PL meaning of the conclusion as existence of a finite collapsible simplicial triangulation whose underlying space is exactly `K.space ×ˢ Set.Icc 0 1`. This does not select or require collapse of a fixed product triangulation and matches the source's equivalent subdivision formulation.

open Geometry

are removed, where `τ` is the unique face of `K` that strictly contains `σ`. -/

    (K L : SimplicialComplex 𝕜 E) : Prop :=
  ∃ σ τ : Finset E, σ ∈ K.faces ∧
    {ρ | ρ ∈ K.faces ∧ σ ⊂ ρ} = {τ} ∧
    L.faces = K.faces \ ({σ, τ} : Set (Finset E))

/-- A geometric simplicial complex is collapsible if a finite sequence of elementary collapses
reduces it to the complex consisting of one vertex. -/
def Collapsible {𝕜 E : Type*} [Ring 𝕜] [PartialOrder 𝕜] [AddCommGroup E] [Module 𝕜 E]
    (K : SimplicialComplex 𝕜 E) : Prop :=
  ∃ L : SimplicialComplex 𝕜 E,
    Relation.ReflTransGen ElementaryCollapse K L ∧
      ∃ v : E, L.faces = {({v} : Finset E)}

The Zeeman conjecture: given a finite contractible two-dimensional CW/polyhedral complex $K$, is

      K.faces.Finite →
      (∀ σ ∈ K.faces, σ.card ≤ 3) →
      (∃ σ ∈ K.faces, σ.card = 3) →
      ContractibleSpace K.space →
      ∃ L : SimplicialComplex ℝ (E × ℝ),

  sorry

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Zeeman conjecture

The Zeeman conjecture (due to Christopher Zeeman) asks whether, for every finite contractible
$2$-dimensional complex $K$, the space $K \times [0, 1]$ is collapsible.

Here "collapsible" is meant in the piecewise linear sense: a compact polyhedron $P$ is
collapsible if *some* triangulation of $P$ collapses to a single vertex by a finite sequence of
elementary collapses (each removing a free face together with the unique face properly
containing it). Equivalently, $P$ is PL homeomorphic to a collapsible simplicial complex, or
some iterated derived (barycentric) subdivision of a triangulation of $P$ is collapsible.
The formalisation therefore does not fix a cell structure on $K \times [0, 1]$. This matters:
Adiprasito and Benedetti showed that for every $m$ there is a finite contractible $2$-complex
$C$ such that the $m$-th derived subdivision of $C \times [0, 1]$ is not collapsible.

Since every compact polyhedron is triangulable, and every finite simplicial complex is
realised in some $\mathbb{R}^n$, the complex $K$ is taken to be a finite simplicial complex in
$\mathbb{R}^n$. A "$2$-complex" is a complex all of whose faces have dimension at most $2$.

The conjecture implies the Poincaré conjecture and the Andrews–Curtis conjecture.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: Zeeman conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeeman_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- K. Adiprasito, B. Benedetti, *Subdivisions, shellability, and collapsibility of products*,
  [arXiv:1202.6606](https://arxiv.org/abs/1202.6606)
- S. Matveev, *Algorithmic Topology and Classification of 3-Manifolds*, Springer (2007), p. 46
- E. C. Zeeman, *On the dunce hat*, Topology 2, 341–358
-/

namespace ZeemanConjecture

open Geometry

variable {E : Type*} [AddCommGroup E] [Module ℝ E]

/-- `ElementaryCollapse K L` says that the simplicial complex `L` is obtained from `K` by an
*elementary collapse*: there is a *free face* `σ` of `K`, i.e. a (nonempty) face `σ` that is
properly contained in exactly one other face `τ` of `K`, and `L` is `K` with the two faces `σ`
and `τ` removed. -/
def ElementaryCollapse (K L : SimplicialComplex ℝ E) : Prop :=
  ∃ σ ∈ K.faces, ∃ τ ∈ K.faces,
    σ ⊂ τ ∧ (∀ ρ ∈ K.faces, σ ⊂ ρ → ρ = τ) ∧ L.faces = K.faces \ {σ, τ}

/-- `Collapses K L` says that the simplicial complex `K` *collapses* to `L`, i.e. `L` is
obtained from `K` by a finite sequence of elementary collapses. -/
def Collapses (K L : SimplicialComplex ℝ E) : Prop :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen ElementaryCollapse K L

/-- A simplicial complex is *collapsible* if it collapses to a single vertex. -/
def Collapsible (K : SimplicialComplex ℝ E) : Prop :=
  ∃ L : SimplicialComplex ℝ E, Collapses K L ∧ ∃ v : E, L.faces = {{v}}

/-- A set `P` in a real vector space is a *collapsible polyhedron* if some (rectilinear)
triangulation of `P`, i.e. some simplicial complex whose underlying space is `P`, is
collapsible. This is collapsibility in the piecewise linear sense: it depends only on the
PL homeomorphism type of `P` and not on any particular triangulation or cell structure. -/
def IsCollapsiblePolyhedron (P : Set E) : Prop :=
  ∃ L : SimplicialComplex ℝ E, L.space = P ∧ Collapsible L

/-- A simplicial complex has *dimension at most `d`* if each of its faces has at most `d + 1`
vertices. -/
def DimLE (K : SimplicialComplex ℝ E) (d : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ s ∈ K.faces, s.card ≤ d + 1

/-- **Zeeman conjecture.** Let $K$ be a finite contractible $2$-dimensional complex. Is the
space $K \times [0, 1]$ collapsible?

Here $K$ is a finite simplicial complex in some $\mathbb{R}^n$ whose underlying space is
contractible and all of whose faces have dimension at most $2$, and "collapsible" is meant in
the piecewise linear sense: some triangulation of the polyhedron
$|K| \times [0, 1] \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n \times \mathbb{R}$ collapses to a single vertex. -/

The Zeeman conjecture (or Zeeman's collapsibility conjecture) asks whether, given a finite
contractible $2$-dimensional complex $K$, the space $K \times [0, 1]$ is collapsible.

Here "collapsible" is meant in the piecewise-linear sense: the polyhedron $K \times [0, 1]$ has
a triangulation that collapses onto a single vertex by a sequence of elementary collapses.

itself need not collapse ([AB12]), so the statement below does not fix any particular cell
structure on $K \times [0, 1]$.

The conjecture implies the Poincaré conjecture and the Andrews–Curtis conjecture.

- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeeman_conjecture)

variable {𝕜 E : Type*} [Ring 𝕜] [PartialOrder 𝕜] [AddCommGroup E] [Module 𝕜 E]

/-- The face `σ` of the simplicial complex `K` is a **free face** of `K` with coface `τ`: `τ` is
the only face of `K` that strictly contains `σ`. -/
def IsFreeFace (K : SimplicialComplex 𝕜 E) (σ τ : Finset E) : Prop :=
  σ ∈ K.faces ∧ τ ∈ K.faces ∧ σ ⊂ τ ∧ ∀ ρ ∈ K.faces, σ ⊂ ρ → ρ = τ

/-- The simplicial complex `L` is obtained from `K` by an **elementary collapse**: `L` is `K` with
a free face `σ` and its unique coface `τ` removed. -/
def ElementaryCollapse (K L : SimplicialComplex 𝕜 E) : Prop :=
  ∃ σ τ, IsFreeFace K σ τ ∧ L.faces = K.faces \ {σ, τ}

/-- The simplicial complex `K` **collapses** onto `L` if `L` is obtained from `K` by a finite
sequence of elementary collapses. -/
def Collapses (K L : SimplicialComplex 𝕜 E) : Prop :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen ElementaryCollapse K L

/-- A simplicial complex is **collapsible** if it collapses onto a single vertex. -/
def Collapsible (K : SimplicialComplex 𝕜 E) : Prop :=
  ∃ L, Collapses K L ∧ ∃ v, L.faces = {{v}}

/-- The coface `τ` of a free face is a facet. -/

theorem IsFreeFace.mem_facets {K : SimplicialComplex 𝕜 E} {σ τ : Finset E}

  obtain ⟨-, hτ, hστ, huniq⟩ := h
  exact ⟨hτ, fun ρ hρ hτρ => (huniq ρ hρ (hστ.trans_subset hτρ)).symm⟩

/-- The coface `τ` of a free face `σ` has exactly one more vertex than `σ`. -/

theorem IsFreeFace.card_eq {K : SimplicialComplex 𝕜 E} {σ τ : Finset E}
    (h : IsFreeFace K σ τ) : τ.card = σ.card + 1 := by

  obtain ⟨-, hτ, hστ, huniq⟩ := h
  obtain ⟨x, hxτ, hxσ⟩ := Finset.exists_of_ssubset hστ
  have hρ : insert x σ ∈ K.faces :=

  exact Set.diff_subset

  LinearOrder.lift' (Fintype.equivFin α) (Fintype.equivFin α).injective

/-- The standard ordered simplicial triangulation of the product with the unit interval. -/
noncomputable def productWithInterval (K : FiniteSimplicialComplex) :
    FiniteSimplicialComplex where
  Vertex := K.Vertex × Fin 2
  fintypeVertex := inferInstance
  linearOrderVertex := finiteLinearOrder (K.Vertex × Fin 2)
  faces := Finset.univ.powerset.filter fun s ↦
    s.image Prod.fst ∈ K.faces ∧
      ∀ a ∈ s, ∀ b ∈ s,
        (a.1 ≤ b.1 ∧ a.2 ≤ b.2) ∨ (b.1 ≤ a.1 ∧ b.2 ≤ a.2)
  empty_mem := by simp [K.empty_mem]
  down_closed := by
    intro s t hs hts
    rw [Finset.mem_filter] at hs ⊢
    refine ⟨Finset.mem_powerset.mpr (Finset.subset_univ t),
      K.down_closed hs.2.1 (Finset.image_mono Prod.fst hts), ?_⟩
    intro a ha b hb
    exact hs.2.2 a (hts ha) b (hts hb)

    FiniteSimplicialComplex where
  Vertex := {s : Finset K.Vertex // s ∈ K.faces ∧ s.Nonempty}
  fintypeVertex := inferInstance
  linearOrderVertex := finiteLinearOrder {s : Finset K.Vertex // s ∈ K.faces ∧ s.Nonempty}
  faces := Finset.univ.powerset.filter fun c ↦
    ∀ a ∈ c, ∀ b ∈ c, a.1 ⊆ b.1 ∨ b.1 ⊆ a.1
  empty_mem := by simp
  down_closed := by
    intro s t hs hts
    rw [Finset.mem_filter] at hs ⊢
    refine ⟨Finset.mem_powerset.mpr (Finset.subset_univ t), ?_⟩
    intro a ha b hb
    exact hs.2 a (hts ha) b (hts hb)

    ℕ → FiniteSimplicialComplex

  ∃ v : K.Vertex,

The Zeeman conjecture (Zeeman's collapsibility conjecture) asks whether, given a finite
contractible $2$-dimensional CW complex $K$, the space $K \times [0, 1]$ is collapsible.

Here "collapsible" is meant in the piecewise linear sense: the polyhedron $K \times [0, 1]$
admits a collapsible triangulation, i.e. it is PL homeomorphic to a collapsible simplicial
complex. It is important not to fix a cell structure on $K \times [0, 1]$: Adiprasito and
Benedetti showed that for every $m$ there is a finite contractible $2$-complex $K$ such that
the $m$-th derived subdivision of the product cell complex $K \times [0, 1]$ is not collapsible,
although some derived subdivision of $K \times [0, 1]$ is collapsible if and only if
$K \times [0, 1]$ is PL collapsible.

The conjecture implies the Poincaré conjecture and the Andrews–Curtis conjecture.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Zeeman conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeeman_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Ze64] Zeeman, E. C. "On the dunce hat." Topology 2 (1964): 341–358.
- [AB12] Adiprasito, K., Benedetti, B. "Subdivisions, shellability, and the Zeeman conjecture."
  [arXiv:1202.6606](https://arxiv.org/abs/1202.6606)
-/

namespace ZeemanConjecture

open Geometry

variable {E : Type*} [AddCommGroup E] [Module ℝ E]

/--
`IsElementaryCollapse K L` means that the simplicial complex `L` is obtained from `K` by an
elementary collapse: there are faces `s ⊂ t` of `K` such that `t` has exactly one more vertex
than `s` and `t` is the only face of `K` properly containing `s` (so `s` is a *free face* of the
facet `t`), and `L` consists of the faces of `K` other than `s` and `t`.
-/
def IsElementaryCollapse (K L : SimplicialComplex ℝ E) : Prop :=
  ∃ s ∈ K.faces, ∃ t ∈ K.faces, s ⊂ t ∧ t.card = s.card + 1 ∧
    (∀ u ∈ K.faces, s ⊂ u → u = t) ∧ L.faces = K.faces \ {s, t}

/-- `Collapses K L` means that the simplicial complex `K` collapses to `L`, i.e. `L` is obtained
from `K` by a finite sequence of elementary collapses. -/
def Collapses (K L : SimplicialComplex ℝ E) : Prop :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen IsElementaryCollapse K L

/-- An elementary collapse of `K` yields a subcomplex of `K`. -/
@[category API, AMS 57]
theorem IsElementaryCollapse.le {K L : SimplicialComplex ℝ E} (h : IsElementaryCollapse K L) :
    L ≤ K := by
  obtain ⟨s, -, t, -, -, -, -, hL⟩ := h
  intro u hu
  rw [hL] at hu
  exact hu.1

/-- If `K` collapses to `L`, then `L` is a subcomplex of `K`. -/
@[category API, AMS 57]
theorem Collapses.le {K L : SimplicialComplex ℝ E} (h : Collapses K L) : L ≤ K := by
  induction h with
  | refl => exact le_rfl
  | tail _ h ih => exact h.le.trans ih

/-- A simplicial complex is *collapsible* if it collapses to a single vertex. -/
def Collapsible (K : SimplicialComplex ℝ E) : Prop :=
  ∃ L, Collapses K L ∧ ∃ v, L.faces = {{v}}

/--
A subset `P` of a real vector space is *collapsible in the PL sense* if it admits a finite
(linear) triangulation that is collapsible, i.e. there is a finite simplicial complex `T` whose
underlying space is `P` and which collapses to a vertex. Equivalently, the polyhedron `P` is PL
homeomorphic to a collapsible simplicial complex.
-/
def IsPLCollapsible (P : Set E) : Prop :=
  ∃ T : SimplicialComplex ℝ E, T.faces.Finite ∧ T.space = P ∧ Collapsible T

theorem isPLCollapsible_singleton (x : E) : IsPLCollapsible ({x} : Set E) := by
  refine ⟨⟨{{x}}, by simp, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩, Set.finite_singleton _, ?_, ⟨_, .refl, x, rfl⟩⟩
  · rintro s rfl
    exact affineIndependent_of_subsingleton ℝ _
  · rintro s t rfl hts ht
    rcases Finset.subset_singleton_iff.1 hts with rfl | rfl
    · exact absurd ht Finset.not_nonempty_empty
    · exact Set.mem_singleton _
  · rintro s t rfl rfl
    simp
  · simp [SimplicialComplex.space]

/-- The empty simplicial complex is not collapsible. -/
@[category test, AMS 57]
theorem not_collapsible_bot : ¬ Collapsible (⊥ : SimplicialComplex ℝ E) := by
  rintro ⟨L, hL, v, hv⟩
  have : L.faces = ∅ := by
    clear hv
    induction hL with
    | refl => rfl
    | tail _ h ih =>
      obtain ⟨s, hs, -⟩ := h
      rw [ih] at hs
      exact hs.elim
  simp [this] at hv

**Zeeman conjecture.** Given a finite contractible two-dimensional CW complex $K$, is the space
$K \times [0, 1]$ collapsible?

Here $K$ is a finite contractible simplicial complex of dimension $2$ in some $\mathbb{R}^d$

meant in the PL sense: the polyhedron $K \times [0, 1] \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R}$
admits a collapsible triangulation, i.e. it is PL homeomorphic to a collapsible complex.
-/

theorem zeeman_conjecture :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (d : ℕ) (K : SimplicialComplex ℝ (Fin d → ℝ)), K.faces.Finite →
      ContractibleSpace K.space → (∀ s ∈ K.faces, s.card ≤ 3) → (∃ s ∈ K.faces, s.card = 3) →
      IsPLCollapsible (K.space ×ˢ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) := by
  sorry

end ZeemanConjecture

face `σ` of `K` which is a proper face of exactly one other face `τ` of `K` (a *free face*; `τ`

removing the two faces `σ` and `τ`. -/
def ElementaryCollapse (K L : SimplicialComplex 𝕜 E) : Prop :=
  ∃ σ ∈ K.faces, ∃ τ ∈ K.faces, σ ⊂ τ ∧ (∀ ρ ∈ K.faces, σ ⊂ ρ → ρ = τ) ∧
    L.faces = K.faces \ {σ, τ}

theorem ElementaryCollapse.le {K L : SimplicialComplex 𝕜 E} (h : ElementaryCollapse K L) :

  obtain ⟨σ, -, τ, -, -, -, hL⟩ := h
  show L.faces ⊆ K.faces
  rw [hL]
  exact Set.diff_subset

        ∃ L : SimplicialComplex ℝ ((Fin n → ℝ) × ℝ),

end ZeemanConjecture
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot table is appropriate; I followed its instruction to read 'collapsible' in the PL sense and not to fix a cell structure on K × [0,1]. The only (minor) note is that the table's parenthetical 'CW/polyhedral complex' had to be resolved in favour of simplicial/polyhedral complexes, since collapsibility is not defined for general CW complexes.
modeling_decisions: The Wikipedia entry says 'finite contractible two-dimensional CW complex'. Collapsibility (and barycentric subdivision, used in Wikipedia's own restatement) requires a polyhedral/simplicial structure, and the conjecture as stated by Zeeman and in the literature (Adiprasito–Benedetti, Matveev) is about 2-dimensional polyhedra / simplicial complexes. I therefore model K as a finite geometric simplicial complex `Geometry.SimplicialComplex ℝ (Fin n → ℝ)` for arbitrary n (every finite simplicial complex embeds linearly in some ℝ^n, and all notions involved are invariant under such embeddings).

'Collapsible' for K × [0,1] is taken in the PL sense, per the decomposition notes: there exists a simplicial complex L in (Fin n → ℝ) × ℝ whose underlying space is |K| × [0,1] and each of whose simplices lies in a prism σ × [0,1] (i.e. L is a subdivision of the prism complex K × [0,1], in the Rourke–Sanderson sense), such that L is collapsible. By Adiprasito–Benedetti (arXiv:1202.6606, 'a complex is PL homeomorphic to a collapsible complex iff some iterated derived subdivision is collapsible', together with the common-subdivision lemma) this is equivalent both to 'K × [0,1] is PL homeomorphic to a collapsible complex' and to 'some iterated barycentric subdivision of K × [0,1] is collapsible' (Wikipedia's restatement). Formalizing general PL homeomorphisms or barycentric subdivisions of prisms would have been much heavier and more error-prone. Note that a fixed cell structure is deliberately NOT prescribed, as required.

'Two-dimensional' is read as 'of dimension at most 2' (`∀ s ∈ K.faces, s.card ≤ 3`). The extra cases (dimension ≤ 1: a point or a tree) are trivially true theorems, so this is equivalent to requiring dimension exactly 2; it also matches the common usage of '2-complex'.

Contractibility is `ContractibleSpace K.space`, i.e. of the polyhedron |K| ⊆ ℝ^n with the subspace topology (which is the standard topology for a finite complex). Since `ContractibleSpace` requires nonemptiness, the empty complex is excluded automatically; the hypotheses are satisfiable (e.g. a single vertex, where the conclusion holds).

Collapsibility is defined combinatorially: an elementary collapse removes a free face σ (a face that is a proper face of exactly one other face τ — τ is then a facet and σ has codimension one, both consequences of downward closure) together with τ; a complex is collapsible if a finite sequence (`Relation.ReflTransGen`) of elementary collapses reduces it to a single vertex (`L.faces = {{v}}`). Finiteness of L is implied by collapsibility.

The bespoke definitions (`ElementaryCollapse`, `Collapsible`, `IsSubdivisionOfProdUnitInterval`) are generic enough that a reviewer might prefer them in `FormalConjecturesForMathlib/`; since the deliverable is a single problem file, they are placed inside `namespace ZeemanConjecture`, with three short API/test lemmas exercising them (an elementary collapse yields a subcomplex; a single-vertex complex is collapsible; the empty complex is not collapsible).
The theorem quantifies over the ambient dimension n inside the statement (rather than having a section variable E) so that `answer(sorry)` is a closed Prop not depending on any parameter.
